description.value: This study examined reward-circuit function and its association with binge-eating behavior in individuals with high BMI during personally relevant high-calorie taste cue exposure using functional MRI.

spans.text: Thus, in the present study, we utilized cues of personal relevance and a Binge Eating Scale (BES) ( ) to test an overlapping model of compulsive overeating that leads to obesity and addiction by examining reward system function in high BMI individuals who exhibit loss of control over eating (i.e., moderate binge‐eating behavior).

description.value: Participants with high BMI and moderate binge-eating behavior were recruited from the general community and completed a single fMRI session.

spans.text: Participants were instructed to eat a typical meal 4 h prior to the scan time, but to abstain from eating after that in order to capture the typical hunger level as one approaches their next meal.

stimuli.value: Personally relevant high-calorie beverages selected from each participant's most frequently consumed high-calorie drink, delivered by mouth, with water as the control cue; visual instructions displayed “high-calorie taste” and “high-calorie swallow.”

spans.text: Examples of the personally relevant high-calorie tastes delivered include Pepsi (100 cal, 0 g fat, 28 g sugar), chocolate milk (210 cal, 9 g fat, 26 g sugar) and cream soda (190 cal, 0 g fat, 31 g sugar).
